title: PhysDox: Benchmarking LLMs on Physical Feasibility Auditing of Physiological Sensing Protocols
abstract: arXiv:2606.05003v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist in experimental design, yet fluent protocols often remain physically infeasible. We introduce PhysDox, a physical feasibility auditing benchmark for biomedical protocols comprising a 683-sample expert-curated Gold set and a 5,000-sample Silver set across six sensing domains. We formulate the task as a two-stage evaluation: severity detection classifying protocols as valid, minor, or fatal, followed by the constraint-level diagnosis of fatal violations. Evaluating 6 LLMs across 4 inference strategies yields a peak Stage-1 macro-F1 of only 53.0. Moreover, strong oracle diagnosis collapses during end-to-end evaluation due to correlated cascade errors. Error analysis reveals scaffold bias, where models conflate procedural completeness with physical validity. translated_title: PhysDox：基于生理传感协议物理可行性审计的大语言模型基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）日益被用于辅助实验设计，然而表面上流畅的协议往往在物理上并不可行。我们提出了PhysDox，这是一个针对生物医学协议物理可行性审计的基准，包含一个由专家精心整理的683个样本的Gold（黄金）数据集，以及涵盖六个传感领域的5,000个样本的Silver（白银）数据集。我们将该任务形式化为两阶段评估：首先是严重性检测，将协议分类为有效、轻微或致命三类，随后对致命违规进行约束层面的诊断。对6个LLM在4种推理策略下的评估显示，第一阶段的最优宏平均F1仅为53.0。此外，即使在有理想oracle诊断的情况下，端到端评估仍会因相关的级联错误而失效。错误分析揭示了“脚手架偏差”（scaffold bias）现象，即模型将程序完整性与物理有效性混为一谈。因此，隐式约束的漏检率是显式硬件违规的2倍，并有强有力的统计证据支持。
tldr: 本文提出PhysDox基准用于评估大语言模型对生理传感协议物理可行性的审计能力，发现现有LLM表现不佳（最高宏F1仅53.0），且存在将程序完整性与物理有效性混淆的“脚手架偏差”，导致隐式约束的漏检率是显式违规的两倍。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PhysDox, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on auditing physical feasibility of physiological sensing protocols, revealing that current LLMs perform poorly (peak macro-F1 of only 53.0) and exhibit "scaffold bias" by conflating procedural completeness with physical validity, causing implicit constraints to be missed twice as often as explicit violations.
